description: Shikigami animation set rows: parallel arrays pairing animation keys (e.g. Idle, AttackA) with AnimMontage asset names.

ID.simple: Shikigami animation-set ID, e.g. CN_010 or CN_010_DAMAGE.
ID.technical: FName row key; ShikigamiDataTable.Id_ShikigamiAnimation[i] names the sets to use. Resolved with FindRow<T> over ShikigamiAnimationDataTables (+0x6E0) by battle preload, battle spawn, capture setup and level sequences; NAME_None entries are skipped by callers. 84 exported rows cover base, damage and per-attack animation sets.

Key.simple: Animation slot/key names (Idle, Run, DashBegin, AttackA...).
Key.technical: TArray<FName> parallel to FileName. Battle spawn walks Key.Num(), skips None keys and calls AnimInstance->SetAnimationAsset(Key[i], Montage, false) with the montage loaded from FileName[i]. Capture setup builds a Key->FileName map for the pose/character capture, filtering by the capture row's idle/enter keys; non-overview captures only keep those two keys. Export example CN_010 starts with Idle, Run, DashBegin, Dash, DashEnd, JumpBegin, JumpUp, JumpTop, Summon, SummonAir,...

Filename.simple: AnimMontage asset names corresponding to Key[i].
Filename.technical: TArray<FName> of montage primary-asset loader keys. Battle preload appends every non-None filename to the montage preload list; battle spawn resolves each through StudioAnimMontageLoaders_810 (0x13946d0) and installs it under the matching Key; capture uses the same names to play idle/pose montages (FileName[0] for the shikigami pose in the capture path). Export example: AM_CN_010_00_Idle_01 for Key 'Idle'. The code indexes FileName by Key.Num() without a length equality check, so malformed rows with fewer filenames than keys are unsafe.

notes: ShikigamiAnimationDataTables is manager slot +0x6E0; registered at GameDataTableManager.cpp:412 and resolved at line 240.

The row is a pure parallel-array mapping; it has no timing, blending or state-machine data. Animation behaviour beyond which montage is installed for a key lives in the anim instance/Blueprint and C++ controllers (not available as Blueprint source here).
There are no localization variants or numbered shards of this table in the export; the 84 rows are different shikigami/attack sets distinguished by ID.

usages.detail: Battle preload joins CharacterShikigami -> Shikigami.Id_ShikigamiAnimation[] -> this row and appends all FileName entries to the montage preload list (retail 0x12bd9b0).
Battle spawn resolves the montage assets and installs each FileName[i] into the shikigami anim instance under Key[i] via SetAnimationAsset.
Character capture builds a Key->FileName animation map (all keys for SituationOverview, idle/enter keys otherwise).
Capture pose playback loads FileName[0] from the shikigami montage loaders and plays it on the spawned shikigami.
